The post Remote Launches Virtual Expense Cards for Global Employees appeared first on Fintech Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
Remote has launched virtual expense cards that let companies manage employee spending alongside payroll.

Remote Expense Cards are available to eligible employees hired through its Employer of Record (EOR) service.

The cards let them pay for work expenses without using their own money or waiting for reimbursement.

Companies can issue virtual cards within one business day in most cases.

They can also set spending limits, restrict purchases and decide who receives a card.

Remote automatically records transactions in its expense management system, where employees can upload receipts through the app.

The cards use existing employment data to help finance teams track spending and apply controls at the point of purchase.

The post Can AI Help Small Businesses Go Global Without a Big Finance Team? appeared first on Fintech Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
Say you run a small business and an order comes in from overseas. You’re happy to take it, but your supplier’s bill is due before the customer’s payment lands.

An exchange-rate move while you wait could leave you with less than you budgeted. You might be doing those sums while packing the next order.

A bigger company has a finance team for that.

Ant International CEO Peng Yang thinks wider access to AI for SMEs could take some of that work off the owner’s desk and give more small businesses a shot at selling abroad.

He called for a new round of “re-globalisation” on a panel titled “Investing in AI for an Inclusive Digital Future” at UN Trade and Development’s World Investment Forum in Doha.

The post TikTok Rolls Out a Standalone TikTok Shop App in Singapore and 3 Other Southeast Asian Countries appeared first on Fintech Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
TikTok has quietly launched a standalone TikTok Shop app in four Southeast Asian markets, Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and the Philippines, TechCrunch reported.

Social media consultant Matt Navarra first spotted the release.

The app, available on iOS and Android, lets users shop through live streams and short videos, get personalised product recommendations, check out in the app, and track orders.

Its store listing also promises free shipping offers, first-order benefits and deals that are only available in the app.

Those exclusive deals give shoppers a reason to buy through the new app rather than the main TikTok app.

TikTok did not respond to TechCrunch’s request for comment, and it is not yet clear whether the company plans to launch the app in more markets.

Southeast Asia is TikTok Shop’s Stronghold

Customers who meet all five qualifying criteria can earn up to 6.01% per annum on their SGD savings, with qualifying activities ranging from salary crediting and card spending to investments, insurance and [...]

The post HSBC Introduces Rewards+ with Up to 6.01% Interest on Savings appeared first on Fintech Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
HSBC Singapore has launched HSBC Rewards+, a programme that pays bonus interest on savings based on a customer’s wider relationship with the bank.

Customers who meet all five qualifying criteria can earn up to 6.01% per annum on their SGD savings, with qualifying activities ranging from salary crediting and card spending to investments, insurance and home loans.

HSBC automatically enrols eligible customers, with no separate registration required. A newly developed rewards engine recognises qualifying activity across transactions, investments, protection and home ownership.

How HSBC Rewards+ calculates bonus interest

The bonus applies to the first S$100,000 of a customer’s average daily SGD balance in a sole-name HSBC Everyday Global Account (EGA), on top of the prevailing base interest rate of 0.01% per annum.

Crediting a monthly salary of at least S$5,000 via GIRO adds 1.50% per annum. Completing at least S$1,000 in qualifying monthly transactions, including eligible card spending, bill payments and PayNow payments to businesses, adds 0.25%.

The post Mr Pips US$61 Million Fraud Case Turns Focus to Vietnam’s Payment Gateways appeared first on Fintech Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
Vietnamese prosecutors have recommended further investigation into how money in the Mr Pips fraud case moved through several payment intermediaries.

Prosecutors outlined the recommendation at the trial in Hanoi this week, as covered by Znews.

On 4 November, a representative of the Hanoi People’s Procuracy told the court that investigators could not fully examine some matters within the time limits.

Instead, they will take them up in a second phase.

This phase will look at the activities of payment intermediaries 9Pay, BigPay, ApotaPay, CPay and HTP.

It will also cover more than 1,400 individuals within the fraud network, to determine their roles and responsibilities.

Authorities have not charged any of the five payment firms in the case.

Inside the US$61 Million Scheme

item.dc:creator: Fintech News Singapore

Visa put 22 AI models through everyday shopping tests, and nearly half of their attempts failed. Its new Agentic Commerce Benchmark tested models from 12 AI labs across 15 shopping scenarios involving TVs, laptops and personal care appliances. The benchmark assessed whether AI models could identify customer needs through conversation and make suitable purchasing decisions. [...]

The post Visa: AI Models Failed Nearly Half of Tests to Make Suitable Shopping Decisions appeared first on Fintech Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
Visa put 22 AI models through everyday shopping tests, and nearly half of their attempts failed.

Its new Agentic Commerce Benchmark tested models from 12 AI labs across 15 shopping scenarios involving TVs, laptops and personal care appliances.

The benchmark assessed whether AI models could identify customer needs through conversation and make suitable purchasing decisions.

They were also expected to avoid making a purchase when no suitable product was available.

More Than Half of Failed Tests Still Ended in a Purchase

Overall, the models achieved a pass rate of 57.2 percent.

The best-performing models passed 82.2 percent of attempts, while the lowest-scoring models passed 28.9 percent.

More than half (54 percent) of failed attempts still resulted in a purchase.

The AI either selected a product that did not meet the customer’s identified requirements or failed to uncover all their needs.

Models that uncovered more customer requirements generally performed better.

The post Tazapay Revenue Jumps 71% as Net Loss Widens to US$7.36 Million appeared first on Fintech Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
Tazapay increased its revenue by 71% in the financial year ended March 2026, although its net loss widened over the same period.

The Singapore-based cross-border payments firm, which Circle agreed to acquire in September, disclosed the results in audited financial statements filed with Singapore’s Accounting and Corporate Regulatory Authority (ACRA), as reported by DealStreetAsia.

Revenue reached US$21.19 million in FY2026, compared with US$12.42 million a year earlier. Net loss widened to US$7.36 million from US$4.28 million, while loss before tax increased to US$6.97 million from US$4.12 million.

Gross profit rises as operating expenses increase

The company’s gross profit grew 77% to US$11.60 million, while cost of sales increased 64% to US$9.59 million, below the rate of revenue growth. Gross margin consequently improved to 54.8% from 52.9% in FY2025.

The post NPCI Expands Beyond Payments With New AI, Blockchain Arm appeared first on Fintech Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
The National Payments Corporation of India (NPCI) is expanding beyond its core payments business with a new subsidiary focused on AI and blockchain.

The new subsidiary, NPCI Tech Solutions Limited (NTSL), will serve as the group’s technology and innovation arm, with a focus on digital financial infrastructure.

NTSL will also develop capabilities in Global Capability Centre (GCC) services.

It will provide technology services for projects such as eKYC Setu, the Unified Ticketing Platform (UTP) and other digital public infrastructure programmes.

The post Yuno Expands Payment Options in APAC, Europe With Ecommpay appeared first on Fintech Singapore.
item.content:encoded:
Yuno has partnered with Ecommpay to expand payment options for merchants operating across Asia-Pacific and Europe.

Through a single integration, Yuno merchants can access more than 100 global and local payment methods, including PayPal, Portugal’s MB Way and Colombia’s PSE.

Merchants can also offer card payments, Apple Pay, Google Pay and instant payment schemes, alongside open banking services in 11 European markets.

The partnership focuses on enterprise merchants in the retail and subscription sectors.
